subject.title: Feature: Inject post-install/update system event into active session

question: Should ClawHub cross the current no-direct-handoff boundary to notify an active OpenClaw session after install/update, and must commands, configuration changes, plugin activation, and restarts require explicit user approval?
rationale: The feature advances setup reliability but changes product ownership and the trust boundary for publisher-controlled content entering trusted session context; current specs deliberately choose inspectable prompts and operator control.

options.title: Consent-gated runtime handoff
options.body: Add an authenticated OpenClaw-owned event API and require explicit approval before every environment-changing setup action.

options.title: Keep explicit setup flow
options.body: Retain copyable prompts and CLI guidance without active-session injection while improving post-install instructions.

options.title: Automatic onboarding execution
options.body: Inject a directive that tells the active agent to read and execute installed SKILL.md setup instructions immediately.

recommendation.title: Consent-gated runtime handoff
recommendation.body: Add an authenticated OpenClaw-owned event API and require explicit approval before every environment-changing setup action.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined current-main code history and explicit collaborator sponsorship for this product decision.
